decision_clause: Ruled out: "letting a grading failure end the run" — because "it makes one flaky model call discard every candidate already screened". Scope: gitseed/pipeline/__init__.py, gitseed/pipeline/run.py, tests/test_pipeline.py; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: The candidate loop in run() still wraps the grader call in a per-candidate try/except that catches any exception, records a run-level reason for that one repository, appends a Reviewed entry with grade=None and a withheld string, and then `continue`s to the next candidate. Nothing in the change re-raises, breaks, returns early, or drops previously accumulated entries when grading fails; the function still returns every screened candidate it built. The only behavioral change is that when the incoming collection is marked incomplete and its stop reason mentions a rate limit, the returned result's rate_limited flag is set to true while the run stays incomplete and keeps its collection-stopped-early reason. The new test asserts exactly that flag alongside the existing incompleteness assertions.
rationale: The decision forbids one specific control-flow shape: a grading failure terminating the run and discarding already-screened candidates. The final tree preserves that shape unchanged — gitseed/pipeline/run.py catches grader.evaluate exceptions per candidate, records them, and continues, and the surviving tests pin the behavior (a grading timeout yields complete=False with the candidate still present and withheld, and a separate test asserts three reviewed entries with the message "one bad repository discarded the others"). The diff touches a different seam entirely: a two-line addition that derives rate_limited from the collection's stop reason, plus one test assertion. It adds no path by which a model call can end the run. I ran the scope's acceptance runner (pytest tests/test_pipeline.py): 25 passed, including both grading-failure containment tests. This is plainly outside the ruled-out approach rather than an ambiguous reading.
